- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.00 or +0.67 in consecutive days), especially in early 30d forecasts.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.33 or 0.00) — model tends to ignore downward momentum.
- Forecast mean reversion too aggressively after sharp spikes — model often overshoots downward after high peaks.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 2–3 days prior) correlates with forecast bias — use sentiment from 2–3 days prior to adjust for momentum.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently overestimates early days (1–5) when sentiment is positive, then underestimates later days (15–30) when sentiment turns negative.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment decay or reversal often triggers underestimation in later forecast days.
- If sentiment is consistently +0.67 or higher for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00 or negative, increase forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect risk aversion.
